card.summary: H.R. 7148, titled the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, became Public Law No. 119-75 on February 3, 2026. This federal law provides funding for the Department of Defense, Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and related agencies for fiscal year 2026. It also sets guidelines for the U.S. Sentencing Commission, extends various healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, and trade programs, introduces pharmacy benefit management transparency rules, and awards a payment to the widow of a late representative.

summary: The Mikaela Naylon Give Kids a Chance Act of 2025 amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to authorize targeted clinical trials using combinations of drugs for pediatric cancer. It also renews the Food and Drug Administration's authority to issue priority review vouchers for sponsors of new products intended to treat rare pediatric diseases until September 30, 2030, and requires the Government Accountability Office and the Department of Health and Human Services to submit reports on the implementation and effectiveness of these provisions.

affected_groups.effect: Must meet modified investigation requirements for molecularly targeted pediatric cancer drugs and become eligible for rare pediatric disease priority review vouchers through September 30, 2030.
affected_groups.group: Drug and biological product sponsors and manufacturers

affected_groups.effect: May experience expedited development of and access to new drug combinations and treatments for rare pediatric conditions.
affected_groups.group: Pediatric cancer patients and patients with rare pediatric diseases

affected_groups.effect: Must issue implementation guidance, process applications under modified rules, resume issuing rare pediatric disease priority review vouchers, and report on implementation efforts.

key_provisions: Authorizes molecularly targeted pediatric cancer investigations involving new drugs used in combination with already approved standard of care active ingredients or adult cancer active ingredients.
Requires the FDA to issue draft guidance on these provisions within 12 months of enactment and finalize it within 12 months of closing the comment period.
Renews the FDA's authority to issue rare pediatric disease priority review vouchers through September 30, 2030, retroactive past its December 2024 expiration.
Updates the due date for priority review user fees to the submission of the human drug application for which the voucher is used.
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on implementation efforts within 6 years.

Requires the Government Accountability Office to conduct studies and report to Congress on the effectiveness of the pediatric cancer drug development changes and the rare pediatric disease priority review voucher program.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Mikaela Naylon Give Kids a Chance Act of 2025 amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to authorize targeted clinical trials using combinations of drugs for pediatric cancer. It also renews the Food and Drug Administration's authority to issue priority review vouchers for sponsors of new products intended to treat rare pediatric diseases until September 30, 2030, and requires the Government Accountability Office and the Department of Health and Human Services to submit reports on the implementation and effectiveness of these provisions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts federal regulation of pediatric cancer research and rare disease drug incentives by allowing new combination drug trials and extending the expired rare pediatric disease priority review voucher program until 2030. These changes alter requirements for drug developers and establish multi-year federal oversight and reporting mandates.
